UX-2 · quick look before any prototype · proposal · 2026-10-20

A5 · Service desk

The Kirridesk look you pointed at, applied to Meridian: a cool blue-grey canvas framing clean white surfaces, hairline cards, one deep emerald for the action, mint for the customer's side of the chat and for anything the assistant wrote, charcoal for Send. Same four screens and the same words as the A4 sheet, so you are only comparing colour and feel. Nothing here is clickable; the full prototype gets built only after you pick. Source: docs/design/DESIGN-DIRECTIONS.md § A5. Fonts load from Google Fonts with a system fallback.

Palette (sampled from the shots; UX-3 makes it exact)

Sampled with Pillow from dr-25 and dr-26: canvas #E5E9F0, app #FFFFFF, side rail #F5F6F7, pills #F3F5F7, AI draft mint #E2F8EF, charcoal button #202629, avatar indigo #2A2663. Two values were darkened because they fail as text: Kirridesk's green #00BC6F carries white text at only 2.49:1, so the button green is #007847 (same hue); its grey captions (#7D878E) are about 3.7:1, so secondary text is #5B656D. Red only for safety. Contrast below is computed from these values, and the build fails if any text pair is under 4.5:1.
